title: RLS-DL: shuffled robust low-bit sieve with about log2 n stages, O(2^(n/L + 27n/L^(3/2)) n^6) work, tolerance 9999/10000 of adaptively placed dephased copies

claims.statement: For every N >= 2 and every s in Z/NZ, with n = ceil(log2 N), the RLS-DL algorithm (shuffled robust low-bit sieve with a number of stages growing with n) with the single parameter rule of proof.md Section 4 (for n >= 4096: l = bitlength(n), R = max(3, l - 2 - isqrt(4l)) stages, b = ceil((n-1)/R) bits per stage, M = b 2^(b + 30 2^R + 5R + 30) leaves per round, G = 2^(G_e) grid guesses with G_e = 15 2^R + 3R + 4, k = 2^32 (G_e + 10) test copies per guess, Q = G(nM + k) copies all acquired before the first measurement, r1 = 200 bitlength(1600(n+1)Q), sort keys of 2 bitlength(Q) + 10 bits, shuffle keys of 2 bitlength(M) + 2b + 70 bits; for n < 4096 the robust exhaustive branch of Section 6.8 with 2^44 copies per candidate) has worst-case total work T(N,s) = O(2^(n/L + 27 n/L^(3/2)) n^6), with L = log2 n, in the challenge cost model (all classical bit operations, circuit generation, gates, measurements, initialisation, sorting and shuffling, the address charge ceil(log2(𝔐+2)) = O(n) per counted operation where 𝔐 = O(2^(n/L + 27 n/L^(3/2)) n^3) is the number of allocated bits plus qubits (proof.md Section 1, cost convention), and n+1 per acquired copy; dominated by label estimation, O(n^4) per leaf over at most Q leaves, where Q < n^2 2^(n/L + 27 n/L^(3/2)) for n >= 4096 (Lemma Env); proof.md Section 8), i.e. uniform envelope B_T(n) = 2^(n/L + 27 n/L^(3/2)) n^6, whose growth index is exactly 1 (proof.md Section 9). This holds on every execution branch, for the clean problem and for every adversary of the globally dephased-copy error model of the fifth claim, jointly with the other three resource bounds and full-secret success probability at least 9/10 (> 2/3) of the same algorithm and configuration (proof.md Theorems 1 and 2). All constants are absolute (independent of N, s, the adversary and all outcomes), though some are very large; inputs with n < 4096 are finitely many values of N with constant cost.

For every N >= 2 and every s in Z/NZ, with n = ceil(log2 N), the RLS-DL algorithm (shuffled robust low-bit sieve with a number of stages growing with n) with the single parameter rule of proof.md Section 4 (for n >= 4096: l = bitlength(n), R = max(3, l - 2 - isqrt(4l)) stages, b = ceil((n-1)/R) bits per stage, M = b 2^(b + 30 2^R + 5R + 30) leaves per round, G = 2^(G_e) grid guesses with G_e = 15 2^R + 3R + 4, k = 2^32 (G_e + 10) test copies per guess, Q = G(nM + k) copies all acquired before the first measurement, r1 = 200 bitlength(1600(n+1)Q), sort keys of 2 bitlength(Q) + 10 bits, shuffle keys of 2 bitlength(M) + 2b + 70 bits; for n < 4096 the robust exhaustive branch of Section 6.8 with 2^44 copies per candidate) has worst-case peak classical space S_C(N,s) = O(2^(n/L + 27 n/L^(3/2)) n^3) bits, with L = log2 n, (sort keys and the rank table, O(Q n) bits, which dominate the current round's records with their shuffle keys, the key counters and the O(n^2) controller; proof.md Section 8), i.e. envelope B_C(n) = 2^(n/L + 27 n/L^(3/2)) n^3, whose growth index is exactly 1. This holds on every execution branch, for the clean problem and for every adversary of the globally dephased-copy error model of the fifth claim, jointly with the other three resource bounds and full-secret success probability at least 9/10 (> 2/3) of the same algorithm and configuration (proof.md Theorems 1 and 2). All constants are absolute (independent of N, s, the adversary and all outcomes), though some are very large; inputs with n < 4096 are finitely many values of N with constant cost.

For every N >= 2 and every s in Z/NZ, with n = ceil(log2 N), the RLS-DL algorithm (shuffled robust low-bit sieve with a number of stages growing with n) with the single parameter rule of proof.md Section 4 (for n >= 4096: l = bitlength(n), R = max(3, l - 2 - isqrt(4l)) stages, b = ceil((n-1)/R) bits per stage, M = b 2^(b + 30 2^R + 5R + 30) leaves per round, G = 2^(G_e) grid guesses with G_e = 15 2^R + 3R + 4, k = 2^32 (G_e + 10) test copies per guess, Q = G(nM + k) copies all acquired before the first measurement, r1 = 200 bitlength(1600(n+1)Q), sort keys of 2 bitlength(Q) + 10 bits, shuffle keys of 2 bitlength(M) + 2b + 70 bits; for n < 4096 the robust exhaustive branch of Section 6.8 with 2^44 copies per candidate) has worst-case peak quantum space S_Q(N,s) = O(2^(n/L + 27 n/L^(3/2)) n^3) qubits, with L = log2 n, (all Q copies of n+1 qubits are held from acquisition until use, plus O(n) ancillas; S_Q <= (n+1)Q + O(n); proof.md Section 8), i.e. envelope B_Q(n) = 2^(n/L + 27 n/L^(3/2)) n^3, whose growth index is exactly 1. This holds on every execution branch, for the clean problem and for every adversary of the globally dephased-copy error model of the fifth claim, jointly with the other three resource bounds and full-secret success probability at least 9/10 (> 2/3) of the same algorithm and configuration (proof.md Theorems 1 and 2). All constants are absolute (independent of N, s, the adversary and all outcomes), though some are very large; inputs with n < 4096 are finitely many values of N with constant cost.

For every N >= 2 and every s in Z/NZ, with n = ceil(log2 N), the RLS-DL algorithm (shuffled robust low-bit sieve with a number of stages growing with n) with the single parameter rule of proof.md Section 4 (for n >= 4096: l = bitlength(n), R = max(3, l - 2 - isqrt(4l)) stages, b = ceil((n-1)/R) bits per stage, M = b 2^(b + 30 2^R + 5R + 30) leaves per round, G = 2^(G_e) grid guesses with G_e = 15 2^R + 3R + 4, k = 2^32 (G_e + 10) test copies per guess, Q = G(nM + k) copies all acquired before the first measurement, r1 = 200 bitlength(1600(n+1)Q), sort keys of 2 bitlength(Q) + 10 bits, shuffle keys of 2 bitlength(M) + 2b + 70 bits; for n < 4096 the robust exhaustive branch of Section 6.8 with 2^44 copies per candidate) acquires exactly Q = G(nM + k) source copies on every branch for n >= 4096 (and Q_s = N 2^44 <= 2^4139, bounded by an absolute constant, for n < 4096), counting every discarded copy and every unused block; for n >= 4096, Q < n^2 2^(n/L + 27 n/L^(3/2)) = O(2^(n/L + 27 n/L^(3/2)) n^2) with L = log2 n (proof.md Section 8), i.e. the full uniform bound with envelope B_samples(n) = 2^(n/L + 27 n/L^(3/2)) n^2, whose growth index is exactly 1, with the same n and success guarantee as the other resources. This holds on every execution branch, for the clean problem and for every adversary of the globally dephased-copy error model of the fifth claim, jointly with the other three resource bounds and full-secret success probability at least 9/10 (> 2/3) of the same algorithm and configuration (proof.md Theorems 1 and 2). All constants are absolute (independent of N, s, the adversary and all outcomes), though some are very large; inputs with n < 4096 are finitely many values of N with constant cost.

Fractional error tolerance epsilon(n) = 9999/10000, for every N >= 2 (no validity threshold; n < 4096 is covered by the branch of proof.md Section 6.8) and every s, under the adaptive globally dephased-copy model of the error_model text (proof.md Section 5): with Q acquired copies at most floor(9999Q/10000) are malformed; the adversary knows N, s, the algorithm and every measurement outcome obtained before each delivery and chooses adaptively which copies are malformed; a malformed copy's first qubit is dephased with respect to all other systems (conditioned on all earlier outcomes, the joint state of that qubit, the rest of the copy, every earlier-delivered copy, the algorithm's workspace and the adversary's system is invariant under its dephasing) and the copy is otherwise arbitrary, possibly entangled with other malformed copies and the adversary's system, but in tensor product with clean copies and the algorithm's systems; every other copy is, at delivery, an independent ideal coset state in tensor product with everything else; the adversary has no access after delivery. For every such adversary, including the one that corrupts nothing (the clean problem), RLS-DL outputs the entire s with probability at least 9/10 (proof.md Theorems 1 and 2), jointly with the four resource bounds of the first four claims, which hold on every branch. The fraction bounds the number of malformed copies among acquired copies; it is not a per-copy corruption probability.

structured.error_model: Adaptive globally dephased-copy model with fraction epsilon(n). Parameters: N >= 2 is the modulus, s in Z/NZ the secret, n = ceil(log2 N), Q the total number of source copies the algorithm acquires, and epsilon(n) the tolerated malformed fraction. Copies are delivered one at a time in acquisition order j = 1, ..., Q. Before copy j is delivered, an adversary that knows N, s, the full description of the algorithm and every measurement outcome the algorithm obtained before copy j is delivered, and that may hold, process and measure an arbitrary private quantum system, decides adaptively whether copy j is malformed; on every execution branch at most floor(epsilon(n) Q) of the Q acquired copies are malformed. A malformed copy is an (n+1)-qubit system (the register shape of an ideal copy, first qubit A followed by an n-qubit register) supplied from the adversary's system, whose first qubit A is dephased with respect to all other systems: conditioned on every outcome of every measurement made before its delivery (by the algorithm or the adversary), the joint state of A, the rest of the copy, every copy delivered before it, the algorithm's workspace and the adversary's system (including every system the adversary later delivers) is unchanged by the dephasing channel w -> (w + Z_A w Z_A)/2 on A, i.e. it has no |0><1| or |1><0| blocks in A. Apart from this a malformed copy is arbitrary: its n-qubit register may be in any state, entangled with the adversary's system and with other malformed copies, and it may depend on all of the information above. Examples are Regev's bad registers |b, x> with b and x arbitrary, mixtures of them, and coset states whose first qubit has fully decohered with no record of the decoherence retained by the adversary. A malformed copy is in tensor product with clean copies, with the algorithm's workspace and with every qubit the algorithm prepares after its delivery (including the qubits that generate its random bits). Every copy that is not malformed is clean: at the moment of its delivery, a fresh ideal coset state rho_s = (1/N) sum_x |psi_{x,s}><psi_{x,s}| in tensor product with everything else (the adversary's system, all other copies and the algorithm's workspace). The adversary interacts with the algorithm only by supplying copies: it learns the algorithm's measurement outcomes as stated above, but after delivery it cannot act on the copy or on the algorithm's quantum or classical systems. All measurements have countably many outcomes. The algorithm is not told which copies are malformed. Quantifiers: the guarantee must hold for every N >= 2 (no validity threshold), every s in Z/NZ and every such adversary, including the adversary that corrupts nothing (the clean problem): the algorithm outputs the entire s with probability at least 2/3, and the four declared resource bounds hold on every execution branch. The fraction bounds the number of malformed copies among acquired copies; it is not a per-copy corruption probability.
